prior_context.question: Approve the implementation plan for EPMCDME-13212 (configurable File Datasource upload limit + batched file saving)?
Code review verdict for EPMCDME-13212 is request-changes (CR-001: storage-namespace TOCTOU race in process_files_batch, major). Approve, request changes, or abort?

prior_orchestrator_verdict.rationale: All three review lenses ran to completion against the full fc9967201..fdec1d4a9 diff. The acceptance lens confirmed all 27 spec-derived criteria pass (config setting, validator wiring, process_files_batch behavior, router/service call sites, tests, and every out-of-scope exclusion). The edge-case lens, with repo read access, found one genuine concurrency defect introduced by parallelizing file writes: a TOCTOU race in the per-user storage namespace creation path (Azure container / GCP bucket / filesystem directory) that can surface as an unhandled 500 on a user's first concurrent multi-file upload (CR-001, major, patch). The blind lens's other 9 observations were cross-checked: the 'no upper bound on the config value' and 'unbounded memory from eager future submission' concerns are the direct, spec-approved consequence of an explicitly out-of-scope design decision ('Enforcing an upper ceiling on the new config value in code' is listed under Out of scope) and are deferred, not blocking. The 'in-flight writes continue after first failure' / 'no cross-file rollback' observations match the spec's own Error Handling section, which explicitly anticipates and accepts this exact behavior change ('this does not regress an existing guarantee'), so they are deferred. 'Only the first exception is surfaced' is a minor UX nuance, deferred. The pre-existing 'JSON validation after write' ordering bug is marginally amplified by concurrency but was not introduced by this diff; deferred. Two test-quality nitpicks (an assertion that exercises stdlib ordering rather than app logic; a mock missing a spec attribute) are dismissed as non-blocking. Standards adjudication: all 6 commits in the review range follow the '<TICKET>: <description>' format required by git-workflow.md; no code-quality or security-pattern violations were found in the diff. Net: 1 patch finding blocks approval; 5 findings deferred with rationale above; 4 dismissed.

standards_review.notes: All 6 commits in the fc9967201..fdec1d4a9 range follow the 'EPMCDME-13212: <description>' subject format.
New code follows existing static-method service pattern; type hints present; no blocking style violations surfaced by any lens.

No secrets, injection, or unsafe file/process handling introduced. The TOCTOU race found by the edge-case lens (CR-001) is a reliability/availability defect (unhandled exception -> 500), not a security bypass, so it is reported as a finding rather than a security standards failure.

findings.problem: process_files_batch submits all files to the thread pool simultaneously (up to 3 concurrent workers). For a user's first-ever upload, the per-user storage namespace does not yet exist, and all three storage backends (AzureFileRepository._get_container, GCPFileRepository._get_bucket, FileSystemRepository.create_directory) use a check-then-create pattern with no concurrency guard: os.path.exists + os.makedirs (without exist_ok=True) for filesystem, and an unguarded create_container/create_bucket call for Azure/GCP.
findings.impact: When 2+ threads in the same batch race past the existence check before either creates the namespace, the losing thread's create call raises (FileExistsError / a cloud-SDK ResourceExists-style error) uncaught. This exception is not a ZipExtractionError, so the router's existing except ZipExtractionError handler does not catch it — it propagates as an unhandled internal error (HTTP 500) instead of a clean, documented failure mode. The old sequential loop never had this race because the first file always created the namespace before the second file's iteration began.
findings.recommendation: Guard namespace creation with idempotent creation (e.g. exist_ok=True for os.makedirs; catch and swallow the cloud-SDK 'already exists' exception in _get_container/_get_bucket) or serialize the first namespace-creation call ahead of dispatching the batch. Add a regression test that drives process_files_batch with a file_repo double whose create-namespace call is not yet idempotent, submits >1 file for a brand-new user, and asserts no unhandled exception.

prior_context.question: Code-review check-round result for EPMCDME-13212's CR-001 fix-up: decision=approve, confidence=high. CR-001 (TOCTOU race in per-user namespace creation across filesystem/Azure/GCP) is resolved. Approve, request further changes, or abort?

prior_orchestrator_verdict.rationale: Targeted re-check of CR-001 (TOCTOU race in per-user namespace creation) against the fix-up diff since reviewed_head=fdec1d4a9502216a364e0549e5a1c86717e7704b. All three storage backends now guard concurrent namespace creation: FileSystemRepository.create_directory calls os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True), removing the check-then-create race entirely (OS-level atomicity); AzureFileRepository._get_container wraps create_container(owner) in try/except ResourceExistsError, falling back to the already-obtained container_client; GCPFileRepository._get_bucket wraps create_bucket(...) in try/except Conflict, falling back to a lazy client.bucket(owner) reference. Each fix is covered by a new regression test that directly exercises the race-recovery path: test_creates_directory_with_exist_ok_to_avoid_toctou_race and test_create_directory_is_idempotent_when_directory_already_exists (filesystem), test_get_container_falls_back_when_created_concurrently (Azure), test_get_bucket_falls_back_when_created_concurrently (GCP). Reviewed the fix-up diff directly (209 lines, 6 files: 3 source + 3 test); it introduces no new security, public-API, data-loss, or build/runtime-correctness risk — the changes are narrowly scoped exception handling plus tests, with no suspicion warranting a blind/edge-case confirmation pass. CR-001 is resolved; no new findings.

finding_status.evidence: FileSystemRepository.create_directory now calls os.makedirs(directory_path_to_create, exist_ok=True), removing the check-then-create window entirely. AzureFileRepository._get_container wraps create_container(owner) in try/except ResourceExistsError, falling back to the container_client already obtained via get_container_client(owner). GCPFileRepository._get_bucket wraps create_bucket(bucket_or_name=owner, location=...) in try/except Conflict, falling back to self.client.bucket(owner). All three fixes are covered by new regression tests exercising the exact race-recovery path (test_creates_directory_with_exist_ok_to_avoid_toctou_race, test_create_directory_is_idempotent_when_directory_already_exists, test_get_container_falls_back_when_created_concurrently, test_get_bucket_falls_back_when_created_concurrently), all confirmed passing alongside the full repository (24 tests) and file-datasource-service/router (129 tests) suites, plus a clean ruff lint pass.
